slides.heading: Comments and Readable Code
slides.body: Comments and Readable Code is part of Introduction to Python and Output. This short lesson gives you a practical Python idea you can understand, try, and reuse in simple programs.

slides.heading: Core Idea: Comments and Readable Code
slides.body: Comments are notes written for humans. Python ignores comments, but they help explain what the code is supposed to do.

slides.heading: Real-World Analogy
slides.body: A comment is like a sticky note beside a task. It does not perform the task, but it helps the reader understand the task.

slides.heading: Example: Comments and Readable Code
slides.code:
# Display a morning greeting
print("Good morning")

annotations.note: This is a comment for human readers. Python ignores it during execution.
This line displays a value or message on the screen.

slides.heading: Key Rule
slides.body: Write one clear instruction at a time. Python reads your code from top to bottom, so order and spelling matter.

slides.heading: Try It Yourself!
slides.prompt: Add a comment, then print the word Done.
slides.hint: Comments start with #. After the comment, write print("Done").

quiz.prompt_text: What does Python do when it encounters a comment (a line starting with #)?

options: It executes the comment as a special command
It displays the comment text on the screen
It ignores the comment completely during execution
It stores the comment in a variable

quiz.explanation: Correct! Python ignores comments during execution. They are notes for human readers only — they help explain what the code is doing without affecting how it runs.

quiz.prompt_text: Arrange the following lines in the correct order to add a comment and then print a morning greeting.
quiz.explanation: The comment describing what the code does is written first, then the print() statement runs to show the greeting. Comments come before the code they describe.

quiz.prompt_text: Write a comment explaining your code, then print the word 'Done' on the next line.

content.hint: Comments start with #. After the comment, write print("Done").

quiz.correct_answer: Any valid Python code that satisfies the prompt.
quiz.explanation: A comment like # Print the word Done is written above, then print("Done") on the next line. Python skips the comment and only runs the print statement.
